First release of the Personal Pages application: personal pages for every XWiki user, along the lines of the
[XWiki Personal Pages design proposal](https://design.xwiki.org/xwiki/bin/view/Proposal/PersonalPages).

## Features

* **Create my personal page** button on the Personal Pages page (`PersonalPages.WebHome`), a **My pages** entry in the
  drawer menu, and a **Personal pages** section in every user profile.
* **All personal pages** table: searchable, sortable and paged, showing only pages the viewer may see.
* **Administration → Users & Rights → Personal Pages**:
  * where new personal pages are created (any page of the wiki),
  * who can read them: all logged-in users (default), only the owner, or the owner and chosen groups,
  * what owners can do: edit, comment, delete, administer (default: edit and delete),
  * **Create missing personal pages** for every existing user, in automatic batches.
* Settings are stored outside the extension, so upgrading or re-importing it never resets them.
* Read access is set on each personal page itself, so it does not depend on the permissions of the page it lives under.
* Works in subwikis, including for users of the main wiki.

## Requirements

XWiki 16.10.0 or later. Tested on XWiki 18.7.0 (main wiki and a subwiki).

## Installation

1. Download `application-personal-pages-1.0.xar` below (optionally check it against the `.sha256` file).
2. As an administrator, go to **Administration → Content → Import**, upload the file, select it, and click **Import**.
   Keep *Import as backup package* **unticked**: the pages must be saved by you so their scripts have the rights they need.
3. Optionally, adjust the settings under **Administration → Users & Rights → Personal Pages**.

Installing through the Extension Manager will be possible once the extension is published on extensions.xwiki.org.

## Known limitations

* XWiki's built-in password login does not accept usernames containing `.`, `@` or spaces (LDAP and OpenID Connect
  users are not affected). Personal pages themselves handle such names.
* In a subwiki, *Create missing personal pages* covers the subwiki's local users; main-wiki users create their pages
  with the button.
* Texts are in English only; they live in `PersonalPages.Code.Translations`.
